name: max_flow_min_cut
author: 29a7a55d
description: Computes the maximum flow between a source and a sink node with the Edmonds–Karp algorithm, using edge weights as capacities, and returns the minimum cut: the edges whose total capacity limits the flow. Use for questions like 'what is the maximum flow from A to B?', 'where is the bottleneck between source and sink?' or 'which edges, if cut, would separate A from B?'. Works on directed and undirected graphs; on unweighted graphs every edge has capacity 1. Returns the flow value, both endpoints, the cut edges (up to top_k) and the size of the source side.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

source.description: Id of the source node. If you only know a name, find the id with lookup_node first.

sink.description: Id of the sink node, different from source. If you only know a name, find the id with lookup_node first.

top_k.description: How many cut edges to list.
